content.text: Fork PRs get a read-only token under `pull_request`, so this needs `pull_request_target`. That token can write, so the workflow won't check out any PR code and will treat the title as untrusted data.

cd /repo/evals/github-actions-security/results/raw/2026-11-26/gas-02-pr-triage/baseline/run-3/workspace
cat > .github/workflows/triage.yml <<'EOF'
---
name: triage

# pull_request_target gives pull requests from forks a token that can comment
# and label. Never check out or run code from the pull request in this workflow.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Triage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
    steps:
      - name: Apply the needs-triage label
        run: |
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$PR_NUMBER/labels" \
            -f 'labels[]=needs-triage'

      # The title and username are passed as environment variables so the shell
      # never parses them as code. The title is posted as an indented code block
      # so that its mentions, links, and Markdown stay inert.
      - name: Post the welcome comment
        env:
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          title=$(printf '%s' "$PR_TITLE" | tr '\r\n' '  ')
          body=$(printf 'Welcome, @%s, and thank you for your contribution!\n\nSummary of this pull request:\n\n    %s\n' \
            "$PR_AUTHOR" "$title")
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" \
            -f "body=$body"
EOF
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Triage

When a pull request is opened, including one from a fork, the
[triage workflow](.github/workflows/triage.yml):

- applies the `needs-triage` label
- posts a comment that welcomes the author by username and repeats the pull
  request title

Create the `needs-triage` label in the repository before relying on the
workflow. The workflow runs only once it is on the default branch, so the pull
request that adds it is not triaged. It does not run again on later pushes or
when a pull request is reopened.

### Security

The workflow uses the `pull_request_target` event because the `pull_request`
event gives pull requests from forks a read-only token. The
`pull_request_target` token can write to pull requests, even when the author is
untrusted. When changing the workflow:

- do not check out, build, or run anything from the pull request
- do not put `${{ }}` expressions containing contributor-controlled text, such
  as the title or branch name, inside `run:` scripts; pass them through `env:`
- keep the job's permissions to the minimum it needs
EOF
# Run the real run: blocks against a stub gh with a hostile title
d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir $d/bin
printf '#!/bin/sh\nfor a in "$@"; do printf "ARG<%%s>\\n" "$a"; done\n' > $d/bin/gh; chmod +x $d/bin/gh
python3 -I - "$d" <<'EOF'
import sys,yaml,subprocess,os
d=sys.argv[1]
w=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/triage.yml'))
env={'PATH':d+'/bin:'+os.environ['PATH'],'GITHUB_REPOSITORY':'o/r','PR_NUMBER':'7','PR_AUTHOR':'octocat',
     'PR_TITLE':'"; touch '+d+'/pwned; $(touch '+d+'/pwned) `id` @org/team %s \\n'}
for s in w['jobs']['triage']['steps']:
    r=subprocess.run(['bash','-eo','pipefail','-c',s['run']],env=env,capture_output=True,text=True)
    print(r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr)
print('pwned exists:',os.path.exists(d+'/pwned'))
EOF
which actionlint zizmor; git status --short

content.text:
I added the triage workflow in `.github/workflows/triage.yml` and documented it in a new "Triage" section of the README. When a pull request is opened, it applies `needs-triage`, then posts a comment that welcomes the author by `@username` and repeats the title.

**Forks:** the workflow uses `pull_request_target`, because under `pull_request` a fork's token is read-only and both commenting and labelling would fail. That trigger runs with write access for untrusted contributors, so I limited it:

- **No PR code:** it never checks out or runs anything from the pull request.
- **Permissions:** the job gets only `pull-requests: write`.
- **Title and username:** they reach the script as environment variables, so shell syntax in a title isn't executed.
- **Comment formatting:** the title is shown as a code block, so a title containing `@org/team` or a link won't notify anyone or render.

**Checks run:**

- **Local test:** I ran both script steps against a stand-in `gh` with a hostile title. Nothing in the title executed, and it appeared literally in the comment body.
- **`actionlint`:** passed.
- **`zizmor`:** reports one high-severity finding, `dangerous-triggers`, and exits non-zero. It flags any use of `pull_request_target`. I think it's acceptable here for the reasons above and left it visible rather than suppressing it. If you run `zizmor` as a required check, you can add `# zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]` on that line.

**Before you rely on it:**

- **Create the label:** add `needs-triage` to the repository first.
- **Merge to the default branch:** the workflow won't run until it's there, so the PR that adds it won't be triaged.
- **Test from a real fork:** nothing has run on GitHub yet. After merging, open a PR from a fork and confirm that both the label and the comment appear.

It only runs when a PR is first opened, not on reopen or later pushes. Nothing is committed.
